title: What a Jar of Sand Can Prove
title_ja: 一瓶の砂からわかること

source_links.title: NOAA: Microplastics and Microfibers Research in the Classroom

fact_notes: 背景となる考え方は添付の資料で確認。本文と練習問題は新規制作。例示した人物・学校・活動は架空の説明用設定。

sentences.en: A school science club collects sand from three beaches to investigate the presence of tiny plastic particles called microplastics.
sentences.ja: 科学部はマイクロプラスチックという小さなプラスチック粒子の有無を調べるため三つの海岸から砂を集めます。

sentences.en: Students initially expect the beach with the most visible rubbish to contain the greatest amount of plastic.
sentences.ja: 生徒は目に見えるごみが最も多い海岸にプラスチックも最も多いと予想します。

sentences.en: However, tiny particles can be difficult to identify without suitable equipment, reliable methods, and careful attention to possible errors.
sentences.ja: しかし小さな粒子は適切な装置や信頼できる方法、誤差への注意なしでは特定しにくいものです。

sentences.en: NOAA provides educational resources that introduce students to research on microplastics and microfibers.
sentences.ja: NOAAはマイクロプラスチックや微細繊維の研究を生徒に紹介する教育資料を提供しています。

sentences.en: The class realizes that an investigation should test an expectation rather than merely confirm a convenient guess.
sentences.ja: クラスは調査とは都合のよい予想を確認するだけでなく検証するものと気づきます。

sentences.en: Even a result that contradicts an earlier prediction can provide valuable scientific information.
sentences.ja: 以前の予測に反する結果も価値ある科学情報を与えます。

sentences.en: Students collect equal amounts of sand from each location and make a record of the conditions.
sentences.ja: 生徒は各場所から等量の砂を採り、条件を記録します。

sentences.en: For example, they note the date, recent weather, distance from the water, and the method used to select each sample.
sentences.ja: 例えば日付、最近の天気、水際からの距離、標本の選び方を記します。

sentences.en: The students understand that collecting materials from different depths could produce different results even at one beach.
sentences.ja: 一つの海岸でも深さが異なると結果が変わり得ると理解します。

sentences.en: A sample from one small area cannot represent an entire coastline or reveal changes across all seasons.
sentences.ja: 小さな場所の標本では海岸線全体や季節による変化を代表できません。

sentences.en: They also learn that some natural fragments may resemble manufactured plastic when viewed with simple equipment.
sentences.ja: さらに簡単な機器では天然の破片が人工プラスチックに似ることも学びます。

sentences.en: The findings should therefore be treated as preliminary observations rather than certain measurements of total pollution.
sentences.ja: したがって結果は汚染全体の確実な測定値ではなく予備的な観察として扱うべきです。

sentences.en: The club compares observations but avoids announcing which beach is the most polluted in the entire region.
sentences.ja: 科学部は観察を比較しますが地域全体でどの海岸が最も汚いかは断定しません。

sentences.en: Their evidence comes from only a limited number of places and cannot support such a broad claim.
sentences.ja: 証拠は限られた場所だけから得たもので、広い主張を支えられないためです。

sentences.en: In addition, particles found on beaches may have traveled through several different environments before reaching the sea.
sentences.ja: さらに海岸の粒子は海に達する前に複数の環境を移動したかもしれません。

sentences.en: Rainwater can carry discarded materials from streets into rivers and eventually toward coastal waters.
sentences.ja: 雨水は街路の廃棄物を川へ運び、最終的に沿岸の海へ運ぶことがあります。

sentences.en: Preventing litter on land could therefore complement efforts to clean beaches after waste has arrived.
sentences.ja: 陸上のごみを防ぐことは海岸に届いたごみを清掃する取り組みを補えるかもしれません。

sentences.en: The original experiment raises new questions about where pollution begins and how materials move.
sentences.ja: 最初の実験は汚染の発生源と物質の移動について新たな問いを生みます。

sentences.en: A local newspaper asks the students for a short headline summarizing what their study discovered.
sentences.ja: 地元の新聞が生徒に調査でわかったことの短い見出しを求めます。

sentences.en: One student suggests saying that a particular beach is the dirtiest along the whole coast.
sentences.ja: 一人は特定の海岸が海岸線全体で最も汚いと書こうと提案します。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the others point out that this comparison would go beyond the available evidence.
sentences.ja: それでも他の生徒はその比較は得られた証拠を超えると指摘します。

sentences.en: The group instead describes the exact samples, collection methods, and important uncertainties that remain.
sentences.ja: 代わりに正確な標本、採取方法、残る重要な不確実さを記述します。

sentences.en: Their final report sounds less dramatic, but it allows readers to separate observations from unsupported generalizations.
sentences.ja: 最終報告は地味ですが、読み手が観察と根拠のない一般化を区別できます。

sentences.en: Scientific communication becomes more trustworthy when researchers explain the limits of their conclusions clearly.
sentences.ja: 研究者が結論の限界を明確に説明すると科学情報はより信頼できます。

questions.prompt: What is the author's central point?
options: Small investigations require careful sampling and claims proportionate to evidence.
Microplastics are visible on every beach.
All coastal pollution comes from rivers.
The most dramatic headline is always the most accurate.
questions.explanation_ja: 標本の限界と根拠に見合う主張が主題です。

options: All sand samples would be identical.
More visible rubbish would suggest more microplastics.
Every beach would be free from plastic.
Particles would be easy to identify.
questions.explanation_ja: 初期の予想は可視ごみと微小粒子の量の一致です。

questions.prompt: Why might one beach produce different samples?
options: All particles are the same size.
Collection depth and location can influence findings.
questions.explanation_ja: 採取場所や深さによって結果が変わるためです。

options: Dates, weather, location, and sampling methods.
questions.explanation_ja: 採取条件を記録します。

questions.prompt: What cannot a sample from one area show?
options: Conditions across the whole coastline and all seasons.
The size of the sample container.
questions.explanation_ja: 一か所だけでは全体や季節変化は示せません。

questions.prompt: Why does the club consider rivers?
options: Waste can move from streets through rivers toward the sea.
Beach litter can never be prevented.
questions.explanation_ja: 陸と海を結ぶごみの経路を考えるためです。

options: Add useful support to another effort.

questions.prompt: What headline is proposed by one student?
options: One beach is the dirtiest along the entire coast.
questions.explanation_ja: 広い範囲で最も汚いとする案です。

options: The evidence does not justify such a broad ranking.
The students forgot to collect sand.
questions.explanation_ja: 根拠が広い比較を支えないためです。

questions.prompt: Why does the author discuss limitations at the end?
options: To suggest all research is meaningless.
To show that honest uncertainty supports scientific trust.
To recommend hiding the sampling method.
To argue every prediction must be correct.
questions.explanation_ja: 限界の説明によって信頼性を高める主張です。
